method: Actual view_image inspection of both contact sheets and all four original 512x512 candidate stills. No new renders or parameter changes.
observations: All four candidate stills show a nonempty stem with several thin, long, separated axial lines; the short overlapping dark clusters in the baseline stem are visibly reduced.
The stem connects the shade and base as a coherent slender support. Its interior remains visibly hatched; the apparent cleanup is not an empty-stem substitution.
The complete shade, stem and base remain inside every original 512x512 frame. Their silhouettes and overall lamp proportions are readily legible.
Three styles remain distinguishable: circumferential curved shade strokes, long axial stem strokes, and short crossed base strokes.
No gross new shade or base alteration is visible in the paired contact sheet. This is a visual observation; numerical isolation must come from separate validation.

At az120 the base front edge retains a conspicuous dark X lattice. At az210/300 the base still has uneven density and open patches. These inherited defects do not obscure the complete object or its three style assignments in these stills.

The stem now looks regular and diagrammatic, with nearly continuous straight parallel lines. Its thin native-resolution footprint leaves limited room to separate hatch lines from silhouette lines visually.

Shade hatches and rim retain some darker stacked strokes and fine raster irregularity, especially az120. The output is a readable GT engineering demonstration, not a polished hand-drawn quality result.
scope_limits: These verdicts apply only to the four exposed static views inspected here.
Orbit, zoom and edit sequences are pending separate actual image review; no motion, flicker, temporal correspondence or video-decode claim is made.
No reconstructed-input, automatic segmentation, general-mesh applicability, user-preference, equal-darkness, H1 or H2 claim is supported by this review.
Inherited hidden-profile observations and previous failures are not resolved by the cleaner stem appearance.
reason_for_bounded_go: The frozen stem edit removes the conspicuous clustered-bar obstacle while keeping visible axial hatch coverage and full-object shape. All three intended part styles are legible in the four stills; residual base/shade imperfections remain disclosed.
